sections.title: Growth & Profitability

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income

sections.subtitle:
Key signals (data to Q1 FY2027, quarter to 30 Jun 2026):
  • Growth is re-accelerating. Net revenue grew 19% in FY2026 and 25% YoY in Q1 FY2027 ($714m); cross-border volume grew 31% and 26%.
  • The margin reset is the big change. Operating margin fell from 36.6% (FY2024) to 23.6% (FY2026) as opex rose to fund compliance, servicing and price cuts. Guidance is an income-before-tax margin at the top of 20-25%; the mid-30s margins are not expected to return.
  • Take rate is falling by design, and more slowly. 0.67% (FY2024) → 0.58% → 0.52% → 0.50% in Q1 FY2027, only −2bps YoY. Volume growth is outrunning the price cuts.
  • About a third of revenue is interest on customer money. Gross interest income was $806m, 32% of FY2026 net revenue. The yield on year-end balances fell from 3.6% to 2.7% as rates fell, but balances grew 36%. Further rate cuts are the main earnings sensitivity.
  • Revenue per customer is flat. About $132 per active customer in FY2026 vs $135-138 in the two years before. Growth now comes from more customers, not from earning more from each one.
  • The balance sheet is mostly customer money. Total assets ($33bn) and reported operating cash flow ($7.6bn) move with customer balances. Read Corporate cash ($1.87bn) and owner FCF instead.
  • Regulatory overhang: Belgian criminal AML probe, the OCC charter denial (Jul-2026) and US securities class actions (class period 11 May - 23 Jul 2026). None of these shows up in the charts yet.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal. Reported FCF here excludes customer-balance flows. FY2026's $637.5m has no matching line in the 20-F (Wise publishes no FCF measure), so treat it as approximate.

charts.title: Shareholders' Equity vs Total Liabilities
charts.annotation: Total assets and liabilities are dominated by customer balances ($30bn at FY2026), which sit on both sides of the balance sheet. Equity is the line that matters.

sections.title: Customers, Volume & Holdings

charts.title: Cross-Border Volume & YoY Growth
charts.annotation: Volume grew 31% in FY2026, faster than revenue (19%), because the take rate was cut.

charts.title: Cross-Border Take Rate
charts.annotation: Down 17bps since FY2024, the price cuts Wise funds from scale. In Q1 FY2027 it fell only 2bps YoY, so the decline is slowing.

charts.title: Customer Holdings: Balances + Assets Under Custody
charts.annotation: Holdings rose 40% in FY2026 to $39bn, and 31% YoY to $41.2bn in Q1 FY2027. Balances earn the interest income; assets under custody earn fees.

charts.title: Interest Income on Customer Balances
charts.annotation: Interest is about a third of revenue. The yield is already falling with rates, and balance growth has so far covered it.

charts.title: Interest Yield on Customer Balances
charts.annotation: 3.6% (FY2024) to 2.7% (FY2026) as central banks cut. Year-end balances overstate the average in a growth year, so the true yield is somewhat higher.

charts.title: Net Revenue per Active Customer
charts.annotation: Flat at about $132-138 since FY2024: growth now comes from adding customers, not from earning more from each one.

sections.subtitle: FY bars are the full-year figures Wise reports: customers active at any point in the year, volume for the year, holdings at year-end. The Q view shows quarterly figures, and customers there are those active in the quarter, so FY customer counts run higher than any single quarter. Pre-FY2025 volumes and balances were reported in GBP and are converted at the same per-year rate used for that year's revenue (FY22 x1.36, FY23 x1.19, FY24 x1.2576).

activeCustomers.title: Active Customers
activeCustomers.content:
Customers who made at least one transaction in the period.

For Wise: the FY figure counts customers active at any point in the year (18.9m in FY2026). The quarterly figure counts customers active in that quarter (11.9m in Q1 FY2027). They are different measures, so compare FY with FY and Q with Q. FY2022 and FY2026 are published only to 0.1m.

What to watch:

  • YoY growth (21% in FY2026, 21% in Q1 FY2027)
  • Business customers, who move about 7-8x more volume per head (FY2024: £50k vs £7.1k)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Wise Group plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Corporate Cash vs Debt
cashDebt.content:
Corporate cash is Wise's own measure of cash it owns, excluding money held for customers. IFRS cash and equivalents is far larger because it includes customer funds.

For Wise: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses Corporate cash ($1.87bn at FY2026, net of borrowings).

What to watch:

  • Corporate cash after the up-to-£405m buyback
  • Regulatory capital surplus (MIFIDPRU 8)

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Wise Group plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Wise Group plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Wise: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross, operating and net margin as % of net revenue.

For Wise: gross margin is net revenue less transaction expense. Operating margin fell from 36.6% to 23.6% over FY2024-26 as Wise raised spending on compliance, servicing and technology. That level is guided as permanent.

What to watch:

  • Operating margin against the 20-25% income-before-tax guidance
  • Servicing + G&A as % of revenue (compliance cost)

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Wise Group plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Wise Group plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Wise Group plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

takeRate.title: Cross-Border Take Rate
takeRate.content:
Cross-border take rate is cross-border revenue divided by cross-border volume: the average price a customer pays to move money between currencies.

For Wise: Wise cuts this on purpose ("Mission Zero") and passes scale savings to customers to win volume. A falling take rate is the strategy working, as long as volume growth stays ahead of it. FY values are Wise's reported annual rates (FY2022-24 from the GBP-era releases; a ratio, so currency does not matter).

What to watch:

  • Volume growth minus take-rate decline (the revenue growth from cross-border)
  • Whether the cuts are voluntary or forced by competitors (stablecoins, Revolut, banks)

volume.title: Cross-Border Volume
volume.content:
Total value customers sent or converted across currencies.

For Wise: volume drives transaction revenue. Before FY2025 Wise reported in GBP; those years are converted to USD at the per-year factor used for revenue, so FY2022-24 levels are estimates (growth within a year is exact).

What to watch:

  • Volume growth against take-rate cuts
  • Business and Wise Platform (bank partner) volume share

holdings.title: Customer Holdings
holdings.content:
Customer holdings = customer balances (cash held on Wise's balance sheet) + assets under custody (customer money invested in funds through Wise Interest/Stocks, held off balance sheet).

For Wise: balances earn interest income for Wise, which keeps the yield above 1% and shares part of it with customers. Holdings growing faster than volume means customers are treating Wise as an account and not only a transfer service, which is the core of the bull case.

What to watch:

  • Holdings growth versus rate cuts
  • Regulatory limits on where balances can be held (safeguarding)

interest.title: Interest Income on Customer Balances
interest.content:
Gross interest earned on customer balances (before the share paid back to customers and interest expense).

For Wise: net of the $196.9m paid to customers, interest was ~$609m in FY2026. The yield line divides by year-end balances, so in a fast-growing year it understates the true yield on average balances. The DCF's owner FCF deducts interest income as non-core, so the valuation does not depend on rates staying high.

What to watch:

  • Yield as central banks cut rates
  • % of revenue: a higher share means more rate sensitivity

revPerCustomer.title: Revenue per Active Customer
revPerCustomer.content:
Net revenue divided by customers active in the year.

For Wise: shown annually only, because quarterly active customers use a different definition.

What to watch:

  • Whether more products per customer (card, account, Assets) lift this back above $140

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
